Happy Wednesday! **Swin** and **Andrew** here. You're right now waking up to a
post-2026 midterms America, and holy _mother of god_ , was that bad… if you
have an "R" next to your name and official title. Was it catastrophically bad
for **Donald Trump** and the Republican Party? Yes. Was it somehow a more
painful night for them than they thought it would be heading into it? Also
yes.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we dive right into the epic conclusion of this
year's high-stakes election cycle, and what the Democratic Party's victories
and the GOP's electoral slaughter mean for the next two years of Trump's
fascist presidency. Plus, we round up some of the night's other key results.

# 'Utter Bloodbath'

Andrew Harnik/Getty Images._

On election night, Mehdi and Prem [livestreamed from
Michigan](https://zeteo.substack.com/p/blue-tsunami-watch-zeteos-coverage).
Andrew was covering Troy Jackson in Maine. And Swin was at the Ohio Democratic
watch party in Columbus, Ohio. All three states are now sending Democratic
senators to Capitol Hill next year - and that was just the tip of the night's
anti-fascist iceberg. Throughout the evening, there was one word that Swin
kept hearing and reading from panicking Republican sources - those in the
Trump-Vance administration, longtime GOP operatives working on competitive
races, big-time conservative donors, and so forth:

"**Bloodbath** ," or, as one Trump adviser put it: "**Utter bloodbath**."

By the middle of the evening, the White House and the larger constellation of
national GOP power knew how bad it was. It was a staggering catastrophe for
the Trump presidency and his MAGA-fied Republican Party - a stunning
repudiation by the American people of President Trump's agenda of senseless
war, ravaged economy, wholesale corruption, and constant barbarism at home and
abroad.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Trump's party lumbered into election night _knowing_ it would be bad, perhaps
even really, very bad. But many of these Republicans, as they told us as the
clock ran well past midnight, were not predicting Tuesday's midterms would be
_this titanic_ of a disaster for the Republican Party. For instance, several
of them told us their worst-case scenarios for Tuesday did not involve Texas
swinging as hard toward the Democrats as the GOP stronghold did on Election
Night.

**" That was worse than we imagined,"** a senior Trump administration official
told Swin in the middle of the night.
